ld.articleBody:
The Court Verdict

A judicial body in Iran has delivered a prison sentence of five years and one month to celebrated director Jafar Panahi in absentia. Legal counsel Mostafa Nili confirmed the decision, stating that the Tehran Revolutionary Court also ordered the seizure of all assets belonging to his client.

In addition to the custodial sentence, the judgment includes restrictive measures preventing the artist from using social media and leaving the nation for a duration of two years. Official state media reports circulating the news omitted specific details regarding the exact nature of the charges.

Discovery of the Conviction

The legal team uncovered the ruling after the filmmaker noticed his financial accounts had been frozen, which led his attorney to investigate at the sentence enforcement office of the Culture and Media Prosecutor's Office. Nili noted that notice of the hearing was never served to the defense.

The lawyer mentioned that his client had traveled back into the country during the military conflict involving Israel and the United States that commenced on February 28. It remains uncertain whether the director is currently residing within the country.

Ongoing Legal Hurdles

This recent ruling adds to a growing list of legal troubles for the 66-year-old artist, who currently faces three active pending cases. Earlier in the year, a judicial rejection dismissed his appeal against a one-year term issued previously for alleged anti-state propaganda.

The international film community continues to monitor his situation closely, as Iranian authorities maintain strict surveillance over prominent artists, creative workers, and media figures whose projects examine societal and political themes.

Festival Accolades and Career Highlights

Despite decades of state-imposed restrictions, the director has maintained a prominent profile on the global cinema circuit. Last year, he earned the top honor at the Cannes Film Festival for his acclaimed motion picture It Was Just an Accident.

His international recognition dates back decades, beginning with his debut feature The White Balloon earning a major honor at Cannes in 1995. Over the years, he has built a reputation for crafting critical perspectives on modern Iranian society.

History of Censorship and Defiance

The auteur has faced persistent friction with authorities, including a twenty-year prohibition on filmmaking and international travel issued in 2010 following his support of anti-government demonstrations. Although initially handed a six-year prison sentence back then, he served only a brief two-month period before gaining release on bail.

Known for finding creative ways to bypass state censorship, he famously smuggled his documentary This is Not a Film out to Cannes hidden inside a cake on a flash drive. His subsequent 2015 project Taxi featured him operating a vehicle as a driver while filming entirely within the cabin, and he endured another lengthy detention in 2022 following filmmaker protests.

News Overview

Iranian authorities sentenced acclaimed filmmaker Jafar Panahi in absentia to over five years in prison alongside property confiscation and multi-year travel and social media bans. The legal development highlights the ongoing challenges faced by prominent artists under strict state surveillance and censorship in the region.

ld.articleBody:
Addressing Character Portrayals

Veteran actor Anupam Kher recently discussed the distinct portrayals of Ranbir Kapoor's Lord Rama and Yash's Ravana in Nitesh Tiwari's ambitious cinematic project, Ramayana. Addressing observations from viewers who found the antagonist's sequences more engaging in the opening chapter, Kher offered a strategic rationale for how the characters were introduced.

Rather than viewing the choices as a misstep, the actor noted that the creative team deliberately elevated the villain to ensure the narrative arc across the planned two-part release carries maximum emotional resonance for audiences worldwide.

The Strategy Behind the Villain

In a conversation with The Hollywood Reporter India, Kher emphasized that director Nitesh Tiwari always intended to split the epic into two parts. Establishing a formidable antagonist early on was crucial for setting the stakes of the overarching conflict between righteousness and malevolence.

Drawing parallels to classic Hindi cinema tropes seen in films like Sholay and Karma, Kher pointed out that building an intimidating and powerful villain is a time-tested method. This deliberate buildup ensures that when the hero ultimately overcomes the adversary in the concluding chapter, the audience experiences a genuine sense of triumph.

The Interdependence of Ram and Ravana

Kher firmly rejected the notion that Ravana inherently steals the spotlight from the central hero, arguing instead that the antagonist's compelling nature stems directly from the character of Ram. While Ravana's presence is inherently dramatic and larger-than-life, Ram's depth unfolds gradually through upcoming sequences.

He cautioned that viewers might be too impatient to judge the complete narrative arc based on the first part alone. Ram's journey, which includes major confrontations and emotional moments, requires patience to fully appreciate.

Humanity and Emotional Depth

To illustrate Ram's emotional core, Kher pointed to specific poignant moments in the film, such as the interaction between Jatayu and Ram where the hero breaks down. It is precisely this display of vulnerability and humanity that moves audiences and grounds the epic tale.

The actor also defended the creative vision of producer Namit Malhotra and director Nitesh Tiwari, dismissing premature criticism from cynics who rush to judgment without understanding the full scope of the planned duology.

Voicing Jatayu

Beyond discussing the broader cinematic strategy, Kher shared insights into his own contribution to the project as the voice of Jatayu. Producer Namit Malhotra personally approached the actor for the voice role, leading to a memorable behind-the-scenes experience.

After being shown a nine-minute preview clip from the film, Kher was so deeply overwhelmed by the visual splendor that he postponed his scheduled recording session by a full day to properly prepare. He ultimately spent five to six hours in the studio perfecting a mere 10 to 12 lines of dialogue.

Production Details and Timeline

Ramayana is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and jointly produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash. The star-studded cast features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana, alongside Anupam Kher voicing Jatayu.

The first part of the cinematic adaptation premiered on November 5, 2026, while the second installment is slated for a 2028 release, continuing the epic mythological journey.

News Overview

Anupam Kher defended the prominent portrayal of Yash's Ravana over Ranbir Kapoor's Ram in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, explaining that establishing a powerful villain in Part 1 is essential for the emotional payoff of good defeating evil in Part 2. Kher also recounted his intense dubbing experience for the character Jatayu in the film, which released its first part on November 5, 2026.

Celebrating a Quarter-Century of Marvel

Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige is honoring 25 years of cinematic history by looking back at the franchise's foundations. Having served as an associate producer on the original 2000 'X-Men' film, Feige is now bringing several of those foundational characters directly into the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

This integration serves as a major milestone for the studio, bridging different eras of superhero cinema. Fans of the early adaptations will see familiar faces transition into a massive crossover event.

Classic Characters Join the MCU

The upcoming fifth Avengers installment will feature several beloved figures from the early 2000s films. Among the returning icons are James Marsden's Cyclops, Rebecca Romijn's Mystique, Professor X, and Magneto.

Bringing these specific iterations into the modern shared universe offers long-time enthusiasts a nostalgic reunion. It connects the classic cinematic mutants with the current roster of MCU heroes.

Fulfilling Long-Time Fan and Actor Hopes

The crossover is something that Hugh Jackman and other talent discussed years ago, noting past obstacles that eventually dissolved. In a recent interview, Feige pointed out that vintage interview clips showed Jackman expressing hope that the X-Men and the Avengers might one day unite.

According to the studio chief, executing this massive crossover simply felt correct. He described the inclusion as an entertaining way to cap off twenty-five years of cinematic storytelling.

Writing Contributions From Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman

The influence of the mutant franchise extends far beyond standard acting roles in the fifth Avengers film. Recent screenwriting credits for the movie reveal that Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman are listed among a group of 10 writers.

These writing credits suggest that the Deadpool and Wolverine actors contributed dialogue specifically for their respective X-Men characters. However, it remains entirely unclear whether they will appear on screen or the exact extent of their physical presence.

Patrick Stewart's Final On-Screen Appearance

The film will also feature the final performance of the late Patrick Stewart as the telepathic mutant mentor, Charles Xavier. This project marks his ninth time embodying the iconic character across his career.

Marvel Studios issued a tribute highlighting his debut in the 2000 film and praising the composure, class, and wisdom he brought to the role. The studio noted that his return for this upcoming movie serves as his absolute final on-screen appearance as the character.

The much-anticipated crossover event is scheduled to hit theaters on December 18, 2026. It stands as a monumental moment for both Marvel Studios and the legacy of early comic book adaptations.

By merging the original mutant cast with the ongoing Avengers saga, the production marks a definitive turning point in superhero cinema history.

Kevin Feige Explains Why Bringing Original X-Men Into 'Avengers: Doomsday' Felt Right

Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige discusses celebrating a quarter-century of Marvel storytelling by integrating classic characters from the 2000s X-Men universe into the upcoming Avengers film.

Published 15 November 2026

Celebrating a Quarter-Century of Marvel

Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige is honoring 25 years of cinematic history by looking back at the franchise's foundations. Having served as an associate producer on the original 2000 'X-Men' film, Feige is now bringing several of those foundational characters directly into the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

This integration serves as a major milestone for the studio, bridging different eras of superhero cinema. Fans of the early adaptations will see familiar faces transition into a massive crossover event.

Classic Characters Join the MCU

The upcoming fifth Avengers installment will feature several beloved figures from the early 2000s films. Among the returning icons are James Marsden's Cyclops, Rebecca Romijn's Mystique, Professor X, and Magneto.

Bringing these specific iterations into the modern shared universe offers long-time enthusiasts a nostalgic reunion. It connects the classic cinematic mutants with the current roster of MCU heroes.

Fulfilling Long-Time Fan and Actor Hopes

The crossover is something that Hugh Jackman and other talent discussed years ago, noting past obstacles that eventually dissolved. In a recent interview, Feige pointed out that vintage interview clips showed Jackman expressing hope that the X-Men and the Avengers might one day unite.

According to the studio chief, executing this massive crossover simply felt correct. He described the inclusion as an entertaining way to cap off twenty-five years of cinematic storytelling.

Writing Contributions From Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman

The influence of the mutant franchise extends far beyond standard acting roles in the fifth Avengers film. Recent screenwriting credits for the movie reveal that Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman are listed among a group of 10 writers.

These writing credits suggest that the Deadpool and Wolverine actors contributed dialogue specifically for their respective X-Men characters. However, it remains entirely unclear whether they will appear on screen or the exact extent of their physical presence.

Patrick Stewart's Final On-Screen Appearance

The film will also feature the final performance of the late Patrick Stewart as the telepathic mutant mentor, Charles Xavier. This project marks his ninth time embodying the iconic character across his career.

Marvel Studios issued a tribute highlighting his debut in the 2000 film and praising the composure, class, and wisdom he brought to the role. The studio noted that his return for this upcoming movie serves as his absolute final on-screen appearance as the character.

Release Details and Legacy

The much-anticipated crossover event is scheduled to hit theaters on December 18, 2026. It stands as a monumental moment for both Marvel Studios and the legacy of early comic book adaptations.

By merging the original mutant cast with the ongoing Avengers saga, the production marks a definitive turning point in superhero cinema history.

News Overview

Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige explained that integrating original characters from the 2000s X-Men films into 'Avengers: Doomsday' felt like a fitting way to celebrate 25 years of storytelling. The upcoming movie features returning actors like Patrick Stewart in his final appearance, alongside writing contributions from Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman.

Set for a December 18, 2026 theatrical release, the crossover successfully unites classic cinematic mutants with the modern Marvel Cinematic Universe.

Key facts

  • Kevin Feige was an associate producer on the 2000 X-Men film.
  • Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on Dec. 18, 2026.
  • James Marsden plays Cyclops.
  • Rebecca Romijn plays Mystique.
  • Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman are among the 10 writers listed for Doomsday.
  • Patrick Stewart is returning for his final movie role as Charles Xavier, marking his ninth time playing the character.
